links.evidence: Both subjects launched as role 'curator' (consumes feature:none, plan:none) wearing only the generic identity. Each persisted adv_sessions.launch_spec has exactly the keys v, role, stack, harnessSlug, workspaceId, stateRevision, specificationArtifact, specificationRevision: no workItem, feature, fleet, launch-slot or assignment key. The compiled configuration's workItem and fleet entries are the pot blueprint's schema sections ({kind: feature, idPrefix: WI} and the worker-role roster), not per-session assignments. The independent subject's coord_presence row has an empty fleet_slug. Its tool refusals name principal system:curator, not a superuser principal.

The snapshot script captures the launcher SU's control_state (modes, route, scope, stack), its agent_modes, its coord_presence role/fleet/fleetRole, the fleet r7-journey-0927 member list, the workspace operator_quota_overrides and the recipe row count. For the independent launch the pre (06:12:23.457Z) and post (06:14:09.109Z) snapshots are identical: zero changed keys. For the fleet-inherited launch (pre 06:08:14.097Z, post 06:11:47.111Z), exactly two keys changed. recipeRows went 0 to 1: the launch provisioned the bundled recipe. fleetMembers gained su-0e27cada. That membership comes from the --fleet=r7-journey-0927 flag capability:launch-agent passes because the launcher leads that fleet; it does not come from the identity, whose launch_spec carries no fleet key. The independent control shows this. The launcher SU's modes, route, scope, stack, presence role and quota rows were unchanged in both runs.

A second turn was delivered to the independent subject at 2026-09-28T06:17:11Z. The event_wake_deliveries row is 382814 with channel psu-socket-inject; an earlier expects:'none' send was suppressed as redundant, see WI-10003578. On that turn the subject's turn-start hooks injected a fresh CTRL block, an Orientation block and a Relevant-memory delta, all without SU assignment fields. It reported CTRL generation 1, wakeSource none, loop inactive, carry warm and no modes. The domain slot still rendered domain:p008-j2-generic-domain under its curator kernel. The recipe was still retrievable, and the subject reported no work-item, loop or file activity.

Neither launch command passes --model. The compiled configuration carries knobs.aiBackend.default.model = claude-opus-4-8 from the identity. Every assistant message in both subject transcripts records message.model = claude-opus-4-8: 8 messages for su-0e27cada and 7 for su-33556642. The independent subject independently reported its runtime model as claude-opus-4-8.

The recipe row count for p008-j2-generic-recipe was 0 before the first launch and 1 after it. Launch provisioning wrote the bundled recipe into harness_shared.code_recipes (authorRole blueprint-bundle). It did not only render the recipe's name into the prompt. Both subjects called recipes:get and got ok with the script text. The independent subject then called recipes:run: ok, summary 'from p008 j2 generic identity', dispatchCount 0, no authority widening.

The generic identity declares no workflow graph. Both subjects launched, and their transcripts show the model choosing its own tool calls turn by turn: coord:whoami, recipes:get and coord:send for su-0e27cada; recipes:get and recipes:run for su-33556642. No workflow step or planner drove them.

The fleet-inherited subject's coord:whoami and coord:send were refused server-side with 'missing_capability: Principal "system:curator" lacks capability "coord:read"' and '... "coord:write"'. The composed identity carried no SU grant: the session kept the curator role's own capability ceiling.

notProven: R-5 coverage is limited to the resource kinds this identity bundles: a callable recipe and a model default. Tool/provider requirements, rubrics, knowledge, and plan/goal/datatype/event/rule resources were not bundled, so they were not driven live here. Their tree-plane coverage is the tests bound on AUTO-BAR-R-5-P-008@3.
'History' and 'addressing' preservation from R-10 were not snapshotted directly. The snapshot covers the launcher's control state, modes, presence, fleet roster, quota overrides and recipe rows.
The subject role was curator, not worker: worker consumes feature:required, and psu refuses to launch it without a feature. A feature-bound role would contradict the no-work-item-state requirement.

summary: Two headless Claude subjects launched on :3170 as role curator wearing only the installed generic identity p008-j2-generic-domain. Their persisted launch specs carry no work-item, fleet or launch-slot fields. An independent launch changed nothing in the launcher SU's state, quotas or fleet. The fleet-inherited launch changed only the fleet roster (from the launcher's own --fleet flag) and provisioned the bundled recipe. Without a --model flag, the identity's bundled model default (claude-opus-4-8) was the model actually used. The bundled recipe reached harness_shared.code_recipes and was callable via recipes:get and recipes:run from the agent's own ReAct loop; no workflow graph was declared. A second turn refreshed the generic identity's context with no SU assignment fields. The curator principal was refused coord:read and coord:write, so composing the identity granted no SU capability.
